pm_exper_user_1469_maasv_v0446_pmv2_r1.question: How can I stop feeling overwhelmed when negative comments about me keep playing over in my head?
pm_exper_user_1469_maasv_v0446_pmv2_r1.all_options:
(a) If you feel stuck looping negative remarks from that highly public policy debate, pause to remember the broader impact of your initiatives and the community voices that value your efforts. Limiting exposure to those threads and seeking balanced feedback from trusted colleagues can help you regain perspective and lessen their hold.
(b) When you catch yourself replaying harsh social media comments from that policy controversy, try to ground yourself in the bigger picture of your work and the constituents you’ve helped. Remind yourself that online reactions are often more about the platform’s dynamics than your worth as a council member, and give yourself permission to step back from those feeds for a while.
(c) When hurtful posts from that public policy dust‑up start running circles in your head, remind yourself that they don’t define your record or the equity‑driven work you champion. Giving yourself space to recharge—maybe at a local farmers’ market or another setting that reconnects you with your community—can help you replace that noise with real conversations.
(d) When negative comments keep replaying in your mind, try to focus on things you know you’re doing well and activities that bring you joy. Taking regular breaks from social media and spending time with supportive people can help shift your attention away from those thoughts.
